public_rationale: GPT-4's documented limitations support Marcus's concern. Other researchers nevertheless described an early version as incomplete AGI. Neither errors nor that label settle his broader proposition. A decisive verdict would depend on an AGI threshold Marcus did not specify, and no cited event meets the early-resolution rule.
limitations: The competing AGI assessment concerns a development version.
This finding does not imply that GPT-4 demonstrated arbitrary-task competence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-4 by itself will not be an AGI capable of arbitrary tasks.

statement.excerpt: GPT-4 by itself won’t be a general purpose artificial general intelligence capable of taking on arbitrary tasks.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

from_speaker: won’t be a general purpose artificial general intelligence

our_interpretation: The target is GPT-4 itself, excluding successor models and systems with additional reasoning or planning tools.
The plain reading is broad competence on unfamiliar tasks across domains, not infallibility or the ability to perform literally every imaginable task.
By itself specifies the evaluated configuration; it is not an antecedent whose future occurrence must be established.
Marcus supplies neither an AGI benchmark nor a required level of performance.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations establish substantial limitations that rule out broadly general task competence under an ordinary reading of the claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reproducible evaluations establish broadly general competence on unfamiliar tasks across domains using GPT-4 without external aids.
